record.context_brief: Central values of weight-2 newform L-functions
record.original_question: Let N be a sufficiently large prime, and let H_2^+(N) denote the set of weight-2 newforms of level Γ_0(N) whose functional equation has sign +1. For each f in H_2^+(N), let L(f,s) be its L-function. Iwaniec and Sarnak proved that, as N tends to infinity, at least 50% of the central values L(f,1) are larger than (log N)^(-2). Is it true that more than 50% of these central values are nonzero?

evidence.quote: Let N be a larger prime, and let H_2^+(N) be set of newforms of weight two for Γ_0(N) whose L-functions have even functional equation. We (Iwaniec-Sarnak) have recently proven that as N → ∞ at least 50% of the central values of L(f,s) for f in H_2^+(N) are larger than (log N)^-2.
Problem A. Show that more than 50% of these central values are nonzero.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a prime number. Let $H_2^+(N)$ denote the set of normalized weight-2 holomorphic newforms $f$ for the congruence subgroup $\Gamma_0(N)$ whose completed $L$-function $\Lambda(f,s)$ satisfies a functional equation with sign $+1$ (i.e., even functional equation). For each $f \in H_2^+(N)$, let $L(f,s)$ denote its Hecke $L$-function, normalized so that the center of the critical strip is $s=1$ (equivalently, after the shift $s \mapsto s+1/2$, the central value is $L(f,1)$).

It is known that, as $N \to \infty$ through primes, at least $50\%$ of the values $\{L(f,1) : f \in H_2^+(N)\}$ exceed $(\log N)^{-2}$; in particular, at least $50\%$ of these central values are nonzero.

Problem: Prove that, as $N \to \infty$ through primes, strictly more than $50\%$ of the central values $L(f,1)$, for $f \in H_2^+(N)$, are nonzero. That is, show that
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\#\{f \in H_2^+(N) : L(f,1) \neq 0\}}{\#H_2^+(N)} > \frac{1}{2}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The 50% non-vanishing result of Iwaniec–Sarnak (Israel J. Math., 2000) remains the benchmark. They showed that breaking the 50% barrier (with central values not too small) would rule out Landau–Siegel zeros, which is why the problem is regarded as very hard. Subsequent works (e.g., on prime power level by Balkanova–Frolenkov and others, and various one-level density investigations) have not surpassed 50% in this family. No proof of strict exceedance of 50% for weight-2 even newforms of prime level appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: The non-vanishing of central values of automorphic L-functions and Landau-Siegel zeros
status_evidence.snippet: Iwaniec and Sarnak showed at least 50% of L(1/2,f) for even newforms are positive, and any improvement is intimately connected to Landau-Siegel zeros.
status_evidence.claim: 50% remains the established proportion; exceeding it is linked to the Landau-Siegel zero problem.

status_evidence.title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions (Sarnak)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of non-vanishing of central values and connection to Siegel zeros.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of strictly exceeding 50% is regarded as connected to deep open questions.

status_evidence.title: Non-vanishing of automorphic L-functions of prime power level
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work on non-vanishing proportions in related families.
status_evidence.claim: Later work has not surpassed the 50% barrier for the weight-2 prime level even newform family.
